result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers meet every rubric item: body size and line-height are in range, line length is capped, .note is raised to 14px, the colors are kept and the heading hierarchy is clear. B centers a readable column by putting max-width and auto margins on the existing .page wrapper. A only caps the p elements, which leaves headings at full width and the text pinned to the left, and A wrongly says centering would need an HTML change. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers meet every rubric item: body size and line-height are in range, line length is capped, .note goes to 14px, colors are unchanged, and the heading hierarchy and spacing are sound. A centers a 68ch column by changing only the CSS on .page, which gives a more balanced page. B wrongly says centering would need an HTML change and leaves the text against the left edge. B's text-wrap additions are a nice touch, but they don't make up for that.
